title: A 250-Year Secret Buried Under a Giant Snake!
summary: Imagine burying a treasure chest that won’t be opened until the year 2276 — that’s 250 years from now! For America’s 250th birthday, all 50 states are stuffing a time capsule with amazing, weird, and wonderful things. It’s like a giant “Message in a Bottle” to the future. What’s inside? Arkansas sent a real diamond! Maine tucked in a bone from an endangered whale. Wisconsin added a feather from “Old Abe,” a bald eagle that helped Union soldiers in the Civil War. And California? They went super sci-fi: a computer chip and an AI-generated guess at what California might look like in 2276. Will there be flying cars? Robot surfers? Who knows! But burying stuff for 250 years is tricky. The team at NIST had to make sure the capsule wouldn’t leak, rust, or get crushed. “Philadelphia would have to be six feet underwater for this to even possibly take on water,” said engineer Michael Berilla. That’s one tough box! It’ll be buried near Independence Hall, where the Declaration of Independence was signed. To mark the spot, they built a giant granite-and-steel snake sculpture — inspired by Benjamin Franklin’s famous “Join, or Die” cartoon. The snake is split into pieces, reminding us that we’re stronger together. Inside the capsule, the very first thing future people will see is a photo of the team and a letter that says, “Greetings from the living, breathing hearts and hands of 2026. We built this for you.” Chills, right? So if you’re around in 2276, grab a shovel and go find that snake. A diamond could be waiting!
why_it_matters: Thinking about the future reminds us that the things we do today will be history one day, and writing letters or burying objects is a way to connect with people long after we’re gone.

background_read: The United States will turn 250 years old on July 4, 2026. To celebrate, all 50 states are sending items to a giant time capsule.
The capsule will be buried near Independence Hall in Philadelphia, the building where leaders signed the Declaration of Independence in 1776.

The snake sculpture at the site is inspired by a famous cartoon by Benjamin Franklin, one of America’s Founders, that showed a snake cut into pieces to mean the colonies needed to join together or die.
Article_Structure: WHO: All 50 U.S. states, the NIST team, and the memory of Benjamin Franklin.
WHAT: A time capsule filled with state treasures being built to last 250 years.
WHERE: Buried near Independence Hall in Philadelphia, next to a giant granite-and-steel snake sculpture.
WHY: To celebrate America’s 250th birthday and send a message to people in 2276.

perspectives.description: It’s a magical way to talk to people 250 years from now. Kids today might have grandkids who open it, or future archaeologists will study it.
Some experts worry the capsule might leak or that future people won’t understand what a computer chip or AI art is.
Time capsules have been buried for centuries, often during big celebrations, as snapshots of what life was like at a particular moment.
